column1: # U5: passwords and 2FA (Bitwarden / Vaultwarden via rbw). Format: see the header of ~/.config/hub/hub.

column9: fzf over your logins. Enter types user, Tab and password into the previous window (wtype, never argv); Alt+p / p password only, Alt+u / u user only, Alt+c / y copies the password (sensitive, clears in 30 s), Alt+t / t copies the TOTP code. The preview shows metadata, never a secret.
Logins with a TOTP key. The preview shows the live code and the seconds left; Enter copies it (sensitive: kept out of the clipboard history and cleared after 30 s).
fzf list with a live code and seconds left: Enter / y copies the code, Alt+t / t types it, Alt+r / r rescans the vault.
Locks rbw and the bw CLI session now; the master password is asked again on the next use. Locked automatically at every login.
Fetches the latest entries from the server (rbw sync, and bw sync when its session is open).
Decodes the export QR (screen region, image or pasted otpauth-migration link) and writes a Bitwarden CSV to $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR for the Vaultwarden web import.

Types the Linux password of the user the focused window asks for, without Enter (sudo and doas: the invoking user, su NAME: NAME, polkit dialog: you, any other terminal process: its user). Needs a Bitwarden folder Linux with one login per Linux user, item name = user name. Only terminals and the polkit agent get typed text; any other window gets a 30 s clipboard copy. An unknown user or a missing item opens a picker.

Fills the Bitwarden folder Linux that SUPER+CTRL+U types from: for every Linux user of this machine (and root) it asks for the password (no echo, Enter skips) and creates the missing login; users that already have an item are skipped. To replace one after passwd, run `linux-pass --update NAME` in a terminal; `linux-pass --list` shows what is stored. Needs the bw CLI login (bw-setup) and asks for the master password once.
